Diagram Studio and the Diagrams menu

Import a draw.io, Visio, SVG, PDF or picture file and rebuild it as an editable SATOM diagram, draw new ones with Flat, Colour or 3D symbols, colour them with themes, gradients and shadows, and publish them in the Diagrams menu, next to the live Architecture and Service Diagram.

What is it?#

Diagram Studio turns a drawing you already have into a native, editable SATOM diagram: a draw.io file, a Visio file, an SVG, a PDF, or even a screenshot or a photographed whiteboard. You can also draw a diagram from scratch. When a diagram is ready you publish it, and it appears in the Diagrams group of the sidebar for everyone who may open it.

A diagram here is a document your team owns (boxes, links, text, layers and versions). The two live diagrams, Architecture and the Service Diagram, sit in the same Diagrams menu with a Live tag, and Open in Diagram Studio on either page copies what it shows into an editable diagram.

What does it do?#

  • Diagrams menu. A first-level sidebar group in every ADOM, directly after Plugin Studio. It holds Diagram Studio, the live Architecture and Service Diagram (each tagged Live), and the published diagrams, in nested folders you create. A folder with nothing published below it is not drawn.
  • Library. A folder tree and a table of every diagram (name, folder, published, updated, owner, elements, versions). The library folders and the menu folders are the same tree; folders nest up to 8 levels and only an empty folder can be deleted.
  • Import. A wizard that reads draw.io, Visio, SVG, PDF, pictures, Mermaid and Graphviz DOT. See Importing files and how recognition works.
  • Editor. Symbols, an inspector, layers, groups, routed connectors, align and auto-layout, search, keyboard shortcuts, autosave, and up to 100 versions with restore and compare.
  • Publishing. Readers see the published version, not your draft.
  • Export to draw.io, SVG, PDF and PNG; a SATOM-exported draw.io or SVG imports back with its classification intact.
  • Symbols in three styles. Flat (217 monochrome icons that take the element's line colour), Colour (158 full-colour icons) and 3D (136 isometric icons), with an isometric grid that snaps 3D icons onto its lattice. One click switches a symbol, a selection or a page between the styles.
  • Colours, effects and themes. Gradients, drop shadows, fill and line opacity and dash patterns in one Style section; ten colour themes that colour a selection, a page or the whole diagram by meaning, with a preview and one undo step. Themes never repaint Colour or 3D icons.
  • Open in Diagram Studio from Architecture and the Service Diagram: an editable copy of what the live page shows.
  • Symbol libraries. The built-in sets above, plus ZIPs of SVG icons that an administrator imports.

Requirements#

  • A profile with the Diagrams keys below. A user without diagrams.view who may open Architecture or the Service Diagram sees a Diagrams group holding only those; a user who may open none of them sees no Diagrams group.
  • For imports, the satom-diagrams service must be running on the node (it is installed and enabled with SATOM; see Importing files).
  • For the vision refinement, an Ollama-compatible local model configured by an administrator (optional).

Permissions#

Key Allows
diagrams.view open the library, the editor (read-only), the published diagrams and the symbol libraries; export what you can see
diagrams.edit create, edit, save, restore, duplicate and delete diagrams and folders
diagrams.import upload files for recognition and review the result
diagrams.publish publish and unpublish diagrams and choose their menu folder
diagrams.libraries import and delete operator symbol libraries (administrators only)

The Read-only profile holds diagrams.view; Operator holds view, edit, import and publish; Administrator holds all five. Creating a diagram from an import needs both diagrams.import and diagrams.edit. These keys stand on their own: they grant no device page. Every write is in the Audit Log as diagram.<verb> (create, save, publish, import_accept, export_drawio, export_svg, export_pdf, and so on).

A diagram belongs to the ADOM it was created in. You see the diagrams of the ADOM you are in; the Global ADOM sees every ADOM's.

How to use#

Draw a new diagram#

  1. Open Diagrams › Diagram Studio and press New.
  2. Drag symbols from the Symbols panel onto the canvas, or use the basic shapes.
  3. Drag from a port dot on a shape and drop on another shape to connect them. Drag the small circle on a segment to add a waypoint.
  4. Press Save (Ctrl+S). Autosave also saves 3 seconds after you stop.

Publish it#

  1. In the library, open the diagram's menu and choose Publish.
  2. Pick the menu folder (or create one). The diagram moves into it.
  3. It now appears under Diagrams in the sidebar. Unpublish removes it from the menu; the diagram stays in the library.

You can keep editing after publishing; readers see the version that was current when you pressed Publish until you publish again.

Use Colour and 3D symbols#

  1. In the Symbols panel, pick Flat, Colour or 3D below Basic shapes. Typing in the search box searches every library; each section then says its style (for example Network · 3D).
  2. For a 3D drawing, choose Isometric grid in the toolbar (next to the grid size). With snapping on, a 3D icon's floor point lands on a lattice point, and waypoints follow the lattice.
  3. To change style later, select a symbol and use Variant (Flat / Colour / 3D) in the inspector's Classification, or, with several items or nothing selected, Switch all to. Connectors stay attached; a style that has no such symbol is disabled, and the message says how many had no variant.

Colour and 3D icons keep their own colours and arrive without a box.

Colour with themes, gradients and shadows#

  1. Press Theme in the toolbar. Choose Selection, This page or Whole diagram, point at a theme to preview it, then press Apply. Ctrl+Z undoes the whole application.
  2. For one item, use the inspector's Style section: Fill, Line and Text palettes, Gradient (Linear with an angle, or Radial), Line width, Line pattern, the three opacities, Shadow, and the font.
  3. Copy style (Ctrl+Alt+C) on one item and Paste style (Ctrl+Alt+V) on others; Reset style goes back to the defaults.

A theme colours each element by its category family (network, security, infra…), else by its shape; zones take their layer's tint and connectors the colour of their kind. It never repaints a Colour or 3D icon: their fill and line stay none and only their label takes the theme's text colour. Your own themes are kept in your browser: Save diagram as theme, Export and Import them as .theme.json files.

Copy Architecture or the Service Diagram into Diagram Studio#

  1. Open Diagrams › Architecture or Diagrams › Service Diagram. On the Service Diagram, expand the devices and set the filters (or search) as you want the copy; the List view must be switched to the Map view first.
  2. Press Open in Diagram Studio (next to Export to; needs diagrams.edit). A new diagram opens in the editor, named Copy of Architecture — or Copy of Service Diagram.
  3. Restyle it like any diagram: a theme, Switch all to 3D or Colour, effects. A line above the editor says when the copy was taken and links to the live page.

The copy is not live: health colours and probe answers are kept only as a snapshot in each element's metadata, and the copy is never updated.

Work with versions#

The clock icon in the editor opens the Version history: each version has its number, date, author and note. Preview one, Restore it (this creates a new version as a copy, so the history is never rewritten) or Compare two versions to see which elements are missing, extra or changed. SATOM keeps the newest 100 versions plus the current and the published one.

Keyboard shortcuts#

Press ? in the editor for the full list. The ones you will use most:

Keys Action
Ctrl+S save now
Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y undo, redo
Ctrl+C / Ctrl+X / Ctrl+V, Ctrl+D copy, cut, paste, duplicate
Ctrl+G, Ctrl+Shift+G group, ungroup
Ctrl+F search elements
Ctrl+Alt+C / Ctrl+Alt+V copy / paste the style of the selection
Delete delete the selection
Arrow keys nudge 1 px (Shift: 10 px); pan when nothing is selected
+ / - / 0 / 1 zoom in, zoom out, fit, 100 %
Enter or F2 edit the text of the selection
Space + drag pan

Configuration#

Export#

Export to (editor toolbar and the published viewer) needs only diagrams.view:

Format What it holds
draw.io every page: shapes, text, colours, containers, connectors with ends, waypoints and routing, custom properties and SATOM's own tags
SVG one page as structured SVG: layers as groups, real <text>, connectors with arrowheads; the full model is embedded, so it imports back exactly
PDF every page as vector paths with real text; fits the diagram, or A4, A3 or Letter
PNG one page as a picture at 1x, 2x or 4x, made in your browser

draw.io, SVG and PDF are written by the server and audited; the PNG is not. Every format draws gradients and shadows as the editor does (draw.io knows only four gradient directions, so an in-between angle is drawn in the nearest one there and comes back exact into SATOM), and Colour and 3D icons keep their colours.

Symbol libraries#

Diagram Studio › Libraries lists the three built-in libraries — Flat (generic), Colour (color) and 3D (iso3d), read-only — and any operator library. An operator library may declare its style (variant: flat, color or iso3d), the floor point of 3D art (anchor) and links to the same concept in other libraries (variants). An administrator with diagrams.libraries imports a ZIP (up to 20 MiB) with an id, a label and a family. Without a library.json in the ZIP, every .svg becomes a symbol. At most 1000 symbols; each SVG at most 64 KiB.

A vendor icon set as downloaded imports as is:

  • Colours the icons set with a stylesheet (<style>.cls-1{fill:…}</style>, the way Illustrator and Inkscape export) are kept. Only plain class rules and the inline style count, and only fill, fill-rule, stroke, stroke-width, stroke-linecap, stroke-linejoin, stroke-dasharray and opacity, with the same value checks as attributes.
  • Icons that draw only in white (the "reverse white" twin a vendor ships of each icon) would be invisible on every theme: they are skipped, with one warning that counts them.
  • A pack whose icons carry their own colours becomes a Colour library: no box behind the icon, listed under the Colour tab of the Symbols panel.
  • Labels keep the file name's capitalisation (FortiGate-Cloud.svg → "FortiGate Cloud").

Example, Fortinet's library: on icons.fortinet.com choose Download All Icons (direct link: https://icons.fortinet.com/Fortinet-Icon-Library.zip), then in Diagram Studio › Libraries import the ZIP, without unpacking it, with id fortinet, label Fortinet icons and family security. The 1578 files become 814 colour symbols; search "FortiGate" in the editor's Symbols panel.

⚠️Warning — Licence of imported icons

SATOM ships only its own original icons. You are responsible for the licence of any library you import: vendor icon packs and stencils are usually under the vendor's terms, and some forbid redistribution or modification.

Example#

A team has an old Visio drawing of its data-centre network. An operator opens Diagrams › Diagram Studio › Import, drops the .vsdx, and reads the result in Review; a vector format is converted exactly, so there is little to fix. After Accept the editor opens; the operator renames two boxes, adds a firewall symbol and saves. Then Publish into a new folder Network › Data centre. Everyone in the ADOM sees it under Diagrams, and anyone with the right can Export to PDF for a design review.

Result#

  • Diagrams, versions and folders are stored in SATOM's database, so the normal database backup covers them.
  • Every create, save, publish, import and export leaves an audit record.
  • A published diagram is visible to every user of the ADOM who holds diagrams.view.

Troubleshooting#

"Conflict" appears in the editor#

Someone saved a newer version after you opened the diagram. Reload to see their changes and re-apply yours; SATOM never overwrites silently.

The Diagrams group is missing from the sidebar#

Your profile lacks diagrams.view and may open neither Architecture nor the Service Diagram. Ask an administrator.

My imported icons came out black, or the import says "the limit is 500"#

The library was imported with an older SATOM, which dropped stylesheet colours and held 500 symbols per library. After the update, delete that library in Diagram Studio › Libraries and import the same ZIP again.

A theme did not colour my 3D icons#

That is intended: Colour and 3D icons keep their own colours. The theme set their label colour only. To colour a symbol, switch it to Flat (Variant).

"Open in Diagram Studio" is missing#

It needs diagrams.edit. On the Service Diagram the List view is not a drawing: switch to the Map view.

Switch all to 3D changed only the small icons#

Elements copied from Architecture or the Service Diagram are boxes with a small icon in their corner; the icon changes style, the box stays.

"Folders nest at most 8 levels deep." or a folder cannot be deleted#

Move the folders up a level, or empty the folder first: only an empty folder can be deleted.

A published diagram looks older than my draft#

That is intended: readers see the version that was current when you pressed Publish. Publish again to update the menu.

For import problems see Importing files and how recognition works.

Advanced#

Advanced Security model

Uploaded files are hostile input and are never parsed by the web process. The web side stores the file and queues a request; a separate, unprivileged satom-diagrams service reads it inside a sandbox with no network, no database and no encryption key. XML DOCTYPE declarations are refused, SVG scripts, foreignObject and external references are stripped, and exports are built from fixed templates. Limits: 20 files and 50 MiB per file, 5 000 elements and 10 000 connectors per page.
